drug_class: ANGPTL3 inhibitor (a type of monoclonal antibody)
purpose: Evinacumab-Dgnb is used to help lower very high levels of LDL cholesterol (the 'bad' cholesterol) in people who have a rare inherited condition called homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH). This condition makes it very hard for the body to remove cholesterol from the blood on its own. It is used along with other cholesterol-lowering treatments, not by itself.
how_it_works: Your body makes a protein called ANGPTL3 that can interfere with how your body breaks down fats in the blood. This medication is a lab-made antibody that blocks that protein, which helps your body process and remove cholesterol and other fats from your bloodstream more effectively. Think of it like removing a roadblock so your body can do its job better.
common_side_effects: Runny nose or nasal congestion, dizziness, nausea, leg or arm pain, and reactions at the infusion site (like redness or swelling where the IV is given) are among the most commonly reported side effects.
warnings: This medication should not be used if you are pregnant, as it may harm an unborn baby — use reliable birth control during treatment and for at least 5 months after your last dose. Tell your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Infusion-related reactions can occur, so you will be monitored during your treatment. Always tell your healthcare team about all other medications you take.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an IV infusion (through a vein) once every 4 weeks, typically over about 60 minutes. It is given in a clinical setting by a healthcare professional. Your doctor will determine the exact dose based on your body weight.
